statement: Let π(p, b) be a probability law with µ = πP , λ = πB. Let E be an allowed set with π(E) ≥ 1 − ζ and suppose 1E(p, b)π(p, b) ≤ Kµ(p)λ(b), K ≥ 1. (2.19) Choose 0 < α < 1 with ζ < 1 − α, retain only point fibers with r(p) := π(E | P = p) ≥ α, and normalize the pairs in these fibers and in E to a law q. Its retained mass M0 satisfies M0 ≥ 1 − ζ 1 − α , q(p, b) ≤ M−1 0 π(p, b), q(b | p) ≤ cλ(b), c := K/α. (2.20) For a fixed integer n ≥ 1, sample B1, . . . , Bn independently given P with kernel q(b | p), and let S(p, b1, . . . , bn) = qP (p) n Y i=1 q(bi | p). The following are comparison probability laws on the whole star: Λ0 = qP ⊗ λ⊗n , S ≤ cn Λ0, (2.21) Λi = qP,Bi ⊗ O j̸=i λBj , S ≤ cn−1 Λi (1 ≤ i ≤ n). (2.22) Here qP,Bi is a copy of the retained pair law q. It may be replaced by the original π in (2.22) at the additional cost M−1 0 . Let R = wS/m, where 0 ≤ w ≤ 1 and m = ESw > 0. Fix an index set J ⊂ {1, . . . , n} of fixed labels; write F = {1, . . . , n} \ J for the free labels. Choose any observation C = (BJ , Z), Z = f(P, BJ ). Thus the function defining Z involves the point and the fixed labels only. For every 0 < η < 1/(n+1), there is a set of C values of RC-mass at least 1 − (n + 1)η on which, simultaneously, R( · | C) ≤ cn mη Λ0( · | C), (2.23) R( · | C) ≤ cn−1 mη Λi( · | C), 1 ≤ i ≤ n. (2.24) 10 For a fixed value C = (bJ , z), put zbJ (p) = f(p, bJ ). Ignoring the deterministic coordinates BJ , these comparison laws are exactly Λ0( · | bJ , z) = qP ( · | zbJ (P) = z) ⊗ O j∈F λBj , (2.25) Λi( · | bJ , z) = qP ( · | Bi = bi, zbJ (P) = z) ⊗ O j∈F λBj , i ∈ J, (2.26) Λi( · | bJ , z) = qP,Bi ( · | zbJ (P) = z) ⊗ O j∈F\{i} λBj , i ∈ F. (2.27) Conditionals in this display need only be defined when their conditioning event has positive comparison mass; the inequalities hold at every R-positive value under consideration. There is also a direct comparison using the actual point marginal. There is a set G of (P, C) values with R(G) ≥ 1 − η such that, for every C value, as an inequality of subprobabilities, 1G(p, C)R(p, bF | C) ≤ c|F| mη RP (p | C) Y j∈F λ(bj). (2.28) For 0 < τ < 1, outside C values of RC-mass at most η/τ, the subprobability on the left has mass at least 1 − τ. In any of these conditionals, all applicable product comparisons, including product comparisons for coordinate tuples at several fixed labels, may be converted simultaneously to comparisons using their actual retained marginals by Lemma 2.6. If the subprobability after all prior trims, including intersection with G when used, has conditional mass u and the resulting list has Nfac factor occurrences, its core has conditional mass at least u/2 and each k-factor comparison constant A becomes at most A(2Nfac/u)k. All exceptional-mass and domination estimates above are independent of the number of possible values of C, P, and the labels.
